title: The Water Cycle
paragraphs: The water cycle is the path water takes as it moves around the Earth. Water is always moving between the land, the sea, and the sky.
Evaporation happens when the sun heats water in seas, rivers, and lakes. The water turns into water vapor, a gas, and rises into the air.
Condensation happens when water vapor cools high in the sky. The vapor turns back into tiny drops of water that form clouds.
Precipitation is water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, or hail. In the Philippines, most precipitation falls as rain during the rainy season. During El Niño, much less rain falls.
After rain falls, some water flows into rivers and back to the sea. Some soaks into the ground. Then the cycle starts again.

text.en: Water moves in a circle. The sun makes water go up. It makes clouds. Rain falls down. Then it starts again.
text.tl: Umiikot ang tubig. Pinapainit ito ng araw at umaakyat ito. Nabubuo ang mga ulap. Bumabagsak ang ulan. Magsisimula ulit ito.

text.en: In the water cycle, the sun heats water so it rises as vapor. The vapor cools and forms clouds. Water falls back as rain and flows to the sea.
text.tl: Pinapainit ng araw ang tubig kaya sumisingaw ito. Lumalamig ang singaw at bumubuo ng ulap. Bumabagsak at naiipon ang tubig, at umiikot itong muli.
